grammar_concept.title: Future Perfect
grammar_concept.rule: Use 'will have + past participle' to talk about an action that will be completed BEFORE a specific point in the future — looking back from that future point, as if it were already the past.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: The Future Perfect lets you talk about a deadline or future moment and describe what will already be finished by then — it's about completion before a point, not just something happening in the future.
grammar_concept.example: By next year, I will have finished my degree. She will have left by the time you arrive.
grammar_concept.example_translation: No próximo ano, já terei terminado a licenciatura. Ela já terá saído quando tu chegares.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: O português tende a usar o futuro simples ou o presente para esta ideia ("no próximo ano termino a licenciatura"), sem marcar gramaticalmente que a ação estará CONCLUÍDA antes de um momento futuro específico. Isso leva a confundir o Future Perfect com o Future Simple ("I will finish" em vez de "I will have finished"), perdendo a noção de conclusão antes do prazo.
grammar_concept.correction: Use "will have + particípio passado" sempre que quiser enfatizar que algo estará terminado antes de um momento específico no futuro ("by [time]", "before", "by the time") — não apenas que vai acontecer algures no futuro.
grammar_concept.real_world_example: Project planning: "By the end of the month, we will have completed the first phase."

vocabulary.translation_pt: até à altura em que, quando
vocabulary.definition_en: used to say something will already have happened before another event
example_sentences: By the time you arrive, I'll have finished cooking.

vocabulary.definition_en: the latest time by which something must be finished
example_sentences: We have a tight deadline this month.

vocabulary.definition_en: to finish doing or making something
example_sentences: We will have completed the first phase by June.

exercises.prompt: Complete: By next year, I ___ (finish) my degree.
exercises.explanation: Conclusão antes de um momento futuro específico ("by next year") — pede Future Perfect: "will have finished".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "will finish" (Future Simple) perde a ideia de que a ação já estará concluída nesse momento, não apenas a acontecer.

exercises.prompt: Complete: She ___ (leave) by the time you arrive.
exercises.explanation: "By the time you arrive" marca um momento futuro — a partida já estará concluída antes disso: "will have left".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "has left" (Present Perfect) em vez de "will have left" ignora que a chegada ainda está no futuro.

correct_answer: the latest time by which something must be finished
exercises.explanation: "Deadline" é o prazo limite para terminar algo.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. What will have happened by the end of the month, according to the speaker?
correct_answer: the first phase will be completed
they will have completed the first phase
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "By the end of the month, we will have completed the first phase."
exercises.transcript: By the end of the month, we will have completed the first phase of the project, assuming there are no major delays.

exercises.prompt: Read: "By the time she turns 30, Ana will have visited more than twenty countries." How many countries will Ana have visited by then?
exercises.explanation: O texto diz diretamente "more than twenty countries".

exercises.prompt: Translate to English: "Até ao final do ano, já terei poupado o suficiente para a viagem."
correct_answer: By the end of the year, I will have saved enough for the trip.
exercises.explanation: Conclusão antes de um momento futuro específico ("by the end of the year") — pede "will have saved", não "will save".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Traduzir para "I will save enough" (sem "have") é o erro mais comum aqui.

steps.content: "Will have" contracts heavily in speech to /wɪləv/ or even /wɪlə/ before a consonant — rarely pronounced as two full separate words in natural conversation.

steps.prompt: Talk about something you will have achieved by a specific point in the future — this time next year, or by a certain age.
Write 3 sentences using the Future Perfect about your own plans, each with a specific future deadline (by next month, by the time you're 40, etc.).
